questions.question: Which element creates a table?
questions.explanation: The table element is used to create a table.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: The <table> element is used to create a table.

questions.question: How is table content written?
options: Column by column with <col> required around each number.
questions.explanation: The contents of the table are written out row by row.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: The contents of the table are written out row by row.

questions.question: What does <tr> mark?
options: The start of a row. tr stands for table row.
questions.explanation: You indicate the start of each row using the opening tr tag. (The tr stands for table row.)

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: You indicate the start of each row using the opening <tr> tag.

questions.question: What does <td> mark?
options: A cell. td stands for table data.
questions.explanation: Each cell of a table is represented using a td element. (The td stands for table data.)

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Each cell of a table is represented using a <td> element.

questions.question: When is the row finished?
questions.explanation: At the end of the row you use a closing tr tag.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: At the end of the row you use a closing </tr> tag.

questions.question: Which heading cell is the usual markup?
questions.explanation: Table headings are th, taught on the pages after the basic structure. Bold td is the look, not the meaning.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: The <table> element is used to create a table.

questions.question: A table of scores should use a table because?
options: Every page layout needs a table.
The information is rows and columns of data.
Images cannot sit on a page otherwise.
questions.explanation: Chapter 6 is how to create tables and what information suits tables — tabular data, not whole-page layout.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett

questions.question: Which snippet matches Duckett's first numeric row?
questions.explanation: Each number is its own td inside one tr.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett

questions.question: Where does an image go if a cell shows a picture?
questions.explanation: The cell holds an img with src and alt. Tables do not grow a src of their own.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Each cell of a table is represented using a <td> element.

questions.question: What is wrong with using one giant table to place a header, nav, and footer?
options: Tables are for tabular data. Page layout belongs to CSS and landmarks.
Browsers delete nested elements inside tables.
questions.explanation: The chapter is how to represent data in tables, not how to scaffold a whole site.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: How to represent complex data in tables

questions.question: How many td elements in a row of three cells?
questions.explanation: It is followed by one or more td elements (one for each cell in that row).

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: It is followed by one or more <td> elements (one for each cell in that row).

questions.question: Which caption placement is the usual one?
options: <caption> as the first child of table.
questions.explanation: A caption belongs with the table element, as a child — not a sibling after the table.

questions.question: Do browsers always draw grid lines for you?
options: Yes, and you cannot change them.
Some draw lines; you control borders with CSS.
questions.explanation: Some browsers automatically draw lines. You control borders of tables using CSS.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Some browsers automatically draw lines around the table and/or the individual cells.
